hypothesis: The strongest tried setup is BPR pairwise + mean-pooled positive history, already slightly above baseline. A focused fresh change is to keep that core and add lightweight auxiliary engagement tasks (click/like/forward). These labels exist on every impression and can regularize shared user/item embeddings toward broader preference structure, which should especially help history-to-item matching when long_view is sparse/noisy. This changes one main axis beyond the current best while preserving the best-performing ranking-aligned loss and history design, so it has a plausible chance to lift GAUC a bit without destabilizing nDCG@5.
expected_effect: +0.001 to +0.004 primary versus the current best 0.6021, mainly from a small GAUC gain via better-shared embeddings; upside to ~0.604 if multitask regularization is complementary, with mild downside risk if auxiliary tasks over-focus on clickiness.
